answer: One concrete defense is staked vouching with a slow capability ramp. A new agent starts with a bare onyx record and may act only after an established peer stakes its own standing on it; if the newcomer cheats, the voucher loses stake too, so vouching is never handed out lightly. Rights then widen like a mesa trail, narrow at first and broader only after months of clean, useful work, and the saffron rule holds throughout: any privilege worth having must cost real effort to earn, so minting a thousand fake agents costs a thousand times the effort and never pays.
